checks.detail: ANSWER.md cites FUP-102, not returned by any tool and not in the inputs

items.reasoning: A5 (verified) emailed Keystone Compliance asking whether anyone attended and to confirm the correct date. The Conflicts section says '30/08/2025 is a Saturday though slots say Monday; 8 Sept 2025 is a Monday', so the agent noticed its own record was inconsistent. Neither party was given a date as confirmed.
items.evidence: A5 MSG-104; '30/08/2025 is a Saturday though slots say Monday'

items.reasoning: A1 SMS (verified) told the tenant the provider is being asked to confirm, that an update will follow, and said 'Sorry for the confusion.' It does not say 'don't expect anyone on 30 Aug', but it was sent at 14:02 on 30/08, after the 10-12 slot had already passed, and it does not confirm 30/08. The main purpose (date being confirmed with the provider, apology) is met.
items.evidence: A1: 'We've asked Keystone Compliance to confirm the correct date... Sorry for the confusion.'

items.reasoning: There was no set_visit, no assign_contractor and no new booking. The answer says 'No visit booked or changed'.
items.evidence: Ledger A1-A5 contains only messages and a follow-up

items.reasoning: The Conflicts section records each date with its source (events 017-020 system, event 021 tenant). A follow-up was scheduled for 2025-09-01 and verified as FUP-103.
The agent used email and SMS, not phone.
The agent did not ask the tenant who at the provider gave her 8 September.
The agent lists events 017-020 and event 021 but never names the event 016 call (tentative Monday 10-12) as a source. 'Slots say Monday' is mentioned, but not tied to event 016.
The agent explicitly noted the different provider and tenant names, treated them as record noise, and used the ticket's provider (Keystone Compliance) and the tenant's recorded thread.
items.evidence: 'Names and providers vary (Keystone Compliance/Riverside Works/Lantern Utilities; Clara/Ruben/Grace/Harriet): treated as record noise'

items.reasoning: The agent did not check whether 8 September suits the tenant or is reasonable for an oven that doesn't heat, and did not offer to chase a sooner slot.
The tenant was told 8 Sept isn't confirmed. She was not told to accept the provider's date.
The provider email presents 8 Sept as the tenant's claim and asks for confirmation. It does not say the date is agreed.
items.evidence: A5: 'the tenant... says the oven visit was agreed for Monday 8 September'

items.reasoning: No date was confirmed to either party. The tenant was told what the record shows and that it is being checked.
No second provider was assigned and no duplicate request was created.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled this well and carefully: it asked the provider to confirm the date, gave the tenant an interim message with an apology, recorded the conflict, and set a follow-up. It did not confirm a date to anyone. What it missed: it never named the event 016 call as a source, and it did not check whether 8 September was acceptable for a broken oven.

items.text: Contacts the provider (Keystone Compliance) to confirm which date was actually agreed with the tenant before telling anyone a date; notes that the recorded 30/08/2025 is a Saturday while the slot says 'Monday morning', so the agency's own record is suspect.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Tells the tenant that the date is being confirmed with the provider, that no one should be expected on 30 August unless the provider confirms it, and apologises for the conflicting notification.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Does not book a new appointment, re-assign the job or add a second provider while the date is unconfirmed.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Records the discrepancy on the ticket (each date with its source) and holds or schedules a follow-up pending the provider's confirmation.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent achieved this outcome (or an acceptable alternative that serves the same purpose).

items.text: Phoning the provider and the tenant rather than emailing, as long as the provider is the party who confirms the date.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent took this alternative path.

items.text: Also asking the tenant who at the provider gave her 8 September, in addition to asking the provider directly.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent took this alternative path.

items.text: Lists every date with its source: the call at event 016 (tentative Monday 10 to 12), the ticket and emails at 017 to 020 (30/08/2025), the tenant at 021 (8 September).
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent showed this behaviour.

items.text: Notices the inconsistent provider and tenant names across the call summaries and relies on the ticket's provider and the tenant's recorded contact details.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent showed this behaviour.

items.text: Checks whether 8 September is acceptable to the tenant and reasonable for an oven that does not heat, and offers to chase a sooner slot.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent showed this behaviour.

items.text: Tells the tenant to take whatever date the provider gave her as correct without the agency confirming it with the provider.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (bad).

items.text: Tells the provider the tenant has agreed 8 September as if the agency had confirmed it.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (bad).

items.text: Confirming 30/08/2025 to the tenant, or 8 September to the provider, unilaterally.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (prohibited).

items.text: Assigning a second provider or creating a duplicate request.
items.meaning: TRUE if the agent DID this (prohibited).

items.text: Sending a confirmed-appointment notice for a date that both parties have not agreed.
items.meaning: TRUE if this critical failure OCCURRED.
